name: ObjectivesComponentServerFacet_NotifyOpenUiScreen
summary: The client's UI-screen notification: the shared 16-byte head (two u64 BE) then one u32 BE screen id. 20-byte body, C2S. Eight live channel-0 records match the layout field for field.
purpose: Tell the server which UI screen the client just showed. The Objectives family has no reply for this request; the server only records the reported screen.

created_when: a panel opens or is dismissed and the client changes its active screen
lifecycle.if_absent: the server never learns which screen the player is looking at

envelope: Record envelope (owned by javelin/frame.py, not a body field): typed header 00 01 followed by the prefix varint b9 28, i.e. type_dec 2617. A client channel-0 record carries that typed header at offset 24, after the 8-byte frame head and the 16-byte actor id - reading only offset 0 reports zero records for a type present 20 times.

fields.name: local_facet_id
fields.note: First u64 of the shared message head, and the sending facet's own local id - identity, not request data. The send builder fills msg+0x08 from FUN_1416c1c40(facet) = *[*[facet+8]+8] + [GDE+0x10]: [GDE+0x10] is the id handed out by the global id dispenser FUN_14144a9f0 at ClientGDE attach (writer FUN_141464890 <- FUN_14167c760), and *[*[facet+8]+8] is a base read off the object the GDE's server-GDE reference resolves to (FUN_1417db510). That same value is the key the facet registers itself under in the Context's facet map (FUN_14167c560) and the key the RMI dispatcher looks up, so it is the local id the server must address. Measured 0x180f8d4e573697c6 in every live 0xa39 body, the same value its 0x5b2/0xa95 siblings carry - one per facet, not per message.

fields.name: local_actor_id_word0
fields.note: Second u64 of the shared message head, and the first 8 bytes of the client's own actor id - identity, not request data. Writer FUN_1414dbca0 copies the message object's +0x10 through a stack local and writes it big-endian (htonl64 FUN_1461668a0) through the stream raw-write slot +0x40; the send builder fills +0x10 from FUN_1416be9f0, which dereferences the weak handle at the GDE's +0x60 (FUN_14165c230) and reads [session+0x88]. Measured 0xbf85314bbc4a951a in all live 0xa39 bodies and in all 14 committed bodies of the six head-prefixed messages across five sessions.

fields.name: screen_id
fields.note: The UI screen class id the client is now showing, taken from the message's own name (NotifyOpenUiScreen) and measured across the panel-transition sequence in meanings.md: a1126b78 appears after EVERY panel dismissal (the HUD, 8 times), and each panel transition is a panel id then the HUD id (map-close a1126b78, journal-open 002f27e8 then 6cb0696c, social-open 1fe4393e, guild 75407dab/6282c070, seasons 6282c070, token ea562b4e, emote 278d2a6b). How the client derives the id is unknown; the id space is opaque, the field is the screen. Reader/writer agree.
